value.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery Token & SameSite Validation Methodology
value.content: {"id": "portswigger_csrf", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "csrf", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)", "name": "Cross-Site Request Forgery Token & SameSite Validation Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-352", "owasp_category": "A01:2021 - Broken Access Control", "signals": ["missing_csrf_token", "static_predictable_token", "csrf_token_not_tied_to_session", "samesite_none_or_absent", "method_override_post_to_get", "referer_header_validation_flaw"], "verification_strategy": "Test state-changing requests (POST, PUT, DELETE) by omitting the anti-CSRF token, supplying an empty token, using a token from an alternate session, and testing HTTP method flipping (POST to GET). Inspect session cookie SameSite flags.", "evidence_requirements": ["successful_state_change_without_token", "cookie_samesite_flags", "csrf_poc_html_form"], "tools": [{"tool": "CSRFSkill", "cmd": "run_csrf_skill(url, param='csrf')", "desc": "Differential state-changing endpoint token omission checker"}, {"tool": "BurpAgent / CSRF PoC Generator", "cmd": "generate_csrf_poc(endpoint, post_body)", "desc": "Creates standard HTML PoC forms demonstrating unauthorized submission capability"}], "remediation": "Enforce cryptographically random anti-CSRF tokens tied uniquely to user sessions. Configure session cookies with SameSite=Lax or SameSite=Strict, and verify custom headers (e.g. X-Requested-With) for AJAX requests.", "description": "PortSwigger CSRF labs demonstrate vulnerabilities where applications fail to validate tokens, accept duplicate tokens from cookie to parameter, bypass token check when omitted, or rely on easily spoofed Referer headers."}
